openDecisions.question: What API should ui/character-card.tsx expose for the stretched link, compact density, secondary name and extra metadata, without changing the edit preview?
openDecisions.specSays: 02: href + linkComponent, a semantic name slot, or an equally small composition API. Stay navigation-agnostic and free of domain knowledge. Keep compact styling opt-in if defaults would alter another consumer. Touch the primitive only if that gives clean composition.
options: A. BookCard-style props. href? + linkComponent? (stretched link, with hover and focus treatment only when href is set), density: 'default' | 'compact' as a cva variant, secondaryName?: string, and meta?: ReactNode appended to the metadata group. The clamp and overflow tooltip live in the primitive and apply only in compact density. The preview passes none of these, so its DOM stays as it is.
B. Slots. nameSlot?: ReactNode rendered inside the h3, plus a meta slot and the density variant. The feature owns the Link, the clamp hook and the tooltip, and the primitive stays hook-free.
C. The roster stops using the primitive and renders its own markup in features/characters. The primitive is untouched.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A mirrors ui/book-card.tsx:37-54, :130, :207-221, which features already use with linkComponent={Link} (list-book-card.tsx:98, series-book-card.tsx:184). B splits the clamp: the h3 that owns the overflow is in the primitive while the measured ref is in the feature, so the ref has to be threaded through or the clamp moved to an inner block. C duplicates the Avatar and initial() markup (ui/character-card.tsx:44-52, :95-97) and leaves two character-card looks that will drift apart.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It follows the precedent the spec names, keeps one card look, and leaves the preview on an untouched default path. Density is a cva variant, not a boolean (code-principles §2.3, §4.7).
openDecisions.answer: A, answered by the user 2026-10-06. Extend the shared ui/character-card.tsx, never a second parallel card. Props: href?: string, linkComponent? (as in BookCard, for the stretched link), density?: "default" | "compact" via cva, secondaryName?: string, meta?: ReactNode. Clamp and overflow-only tooltip are centralised in the primitive. meta stays a pure presentation slot: the primitive knows nothing about appearanceCount, tags or other domain data. Follow-up clarification (same day): density="compact" applies ONLY to the Book Details roster. default stays for the Character Edit preview and the existing UI/CharacterCard stories with no visual refactor. The global /characters catalog is NOT moved onto the primitive in this diff (its DOM, grid/list cards, tags/meta and skeletons stay untouched); shape the API so that move is painless later, and record it as a follow-up.

openDecisions.question: Should the new name link keep the overlay's aria-label 'Відкрити персонажа {name}' (character-card.tsx:131)?
openDecisions.specSays: 02: character navigation stays a real link, and visual clipping never replaces the full accessible character name. The spec does not say what the label text should be.
options: A. No aria-label. The link's name is the full visible name, and the h3's name stays the character name. One assertion changes: character-card.test.tsx:69 becomes getByRole('link', { name: 'Ґеральт' }).

B. Keep the aria-label on the link. The h3's computed name becomes 'Відкрити персонажа Ґеральт', which breaks 37 heading lookups in book-characters-tab.test.tsx (including cardFor at :62-66) and character-card.test.tsx:33. Screen-reader heading navigation would also read the verb on every card.
C. An sr-only 'Відкрити персонажа' prefix inside the link. The heading name changes the same way as in B.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A changes 1 assertion. B and C change 38.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It matches BookCard, BookRow and PublisherCard, where the link's name is the title (ui/book-card.tsx:216-221, publisher-card.tsx:35-40). characters.card.openDetails then has no consumer left (D5).
openDecisions.answer: A, adopted as recommended (user did not object). No aria-label on the name link; its accessible name is the full visible name.

openDecisions.question: The original bug exists only while the card is under a real pointer (:hover triggers the transform). storybook/test userEvent produces neither :hover nor hit-testing (audit C8). How should the browser proof click?
openDecisions.specSays: 03 §1: use the existing browser-capable Storybook/Vitest harness or an equivalent already-supported browser test, and prove five interactions. 00: JSDOM is insufficient.
options: A. A Storybook story with storybook/test userEvent, plus document.elementFromPoint checks at the control centres. Cheap, but it passes on the unfixed code: without :hover there is no transform, so the actions' z-20 wins. It is not a regression test.

B. A Storybook story whose play function clicks through Vitest's provider-backed userEvent from 'vitest/browser' (Vitest 4.1.10 exports ./browser). A real Playwright pointer produces real :hover, and Playwright's actionability check fails when another element intercepts the click. Unverified: whether a story module that imports 'vitest/browser' still loads in `storybook dev`. That needs a Context7 check, and the import may have to sit in a test-only story file.

C. A dedicated *.browser.test.tsx run by a new browser project in apps/web/vitest.config.ts (excluded from unit), using 'vitest/browser' page and userEvent. It is a real browser, but it changes the Vitest config and must rebuild what .storybook/preview.tsx already wires: globals.css, next-intl, Query, nuqs, Tooltip and the next/navigation mocks.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A reuses everything but proves nothing about this bug. B reuses the storybook project (vitest.config.ts:56-68) and the preview providers. C adds a third Vitest project.
openDecisions.recommendation: B, with an acceptance gate: the ⋮ and Favorite proofs must be seen failing against the unfixed character-card.tsx before T7 lands. If 'vitest/browser' cannot load in a play function, fall back to C. Add A's elementFromPoint checks in every case, because they are cheap and state the hit-test intent. Render the full BookCharactersTab with globalThis.fetch mocked so Favorite can visibly flip (audit C12). Record navigation with a capture-phase click listener on the story root that calls preventDefault and stores the anchor href, unless Context7 confirms that the mocked router in @storybook/nextjs-vite intercepts next-intl Link clicks.
openDecisions.answer: B, answered by the user. Use the existing storybook browser project in apps/web/vitest.config.ts (Playwright/Chromium). No separate vitest.browser config, no new test infrastructure. The regression story/play test must use a real browser pointer (provider-backed userEvent from vitest/browser), reproduce the bug on the old implementation first (red), then pass after the fix. Cover: hover with a real pointer, then click the kebab opens the menu and does not navigate; a click on an ordinary card area navigates to the href; document.elementFromPoint() at the action controls proves the action sits above the stretched link. Never prove this with happy-dom or with storybook/test userEvent alone. After the fix the story also asserts hover/focus cause no physical card shift.

openDecisions.question: Where should the hover lift go away: only for the roster, or in the primitive's default?
openDecisions.specSays: 01 §6: the roster card has no vertical translate, and removing it is intentional. 01 §5: roster styling is opt-in if a default change would alter another consumer.
options: A. Keep the primitive's default (hover:-translate-y-0.5 with transition on transform), and cancel it from the roster with a hover:translate-y-0 override, as the preview does (character-edit-preview.tsx:57).

B. Remove the lift from the primitive's base classes, and apply the hover and focus border and shadow only when href is set, like BookCard's interactive variant (ui/book-card.tsx:17-35). The preview has no href and keeps the no-hover look its override already gives it. The UI/CharacterCard stories lose their lift.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A leaves a translate utility on the roster card and a lift in the primitive that every consumer has to cancel. B changes one class string, and the preview's override becomes redundant but harmless (no edit to the preview).
openDecisions.recommendation: B. No Book Nest clickable card lifts (audit C24). The primitive's lift exists only to be cancelled by its one product consumer outside the roster.
openDecisions.answer: B, answered by the user. Remove hover:-translate-y-0.5 (and the transform transition) from the primitive base classes. Keep hover:shadow-hover, hover:border-accent-border where needed, and focus-visible styles for the interactive card. Do not add a compensating hover:translate-y-0 in the roster. Hover behaviour is one for every use of the primitive.

openDecisions.question: 03 §5 and §6 list `pnpm --filter @app/web test`. CLAUDE.md §9 makes a local full suite opt-in and leaves it to CI (ci.yml:179 runs exactly this command). Should it run locally?
options: A. Run it locally once at the end with VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2, treating the spec as the user's explicit request.
B. Run only the focused files locally and rely on CI after the push.

openDecisions.answer: A, answered by the user. Focused tests during implementation. Before the final report run VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 pnpm --filter @app/web test and pnpm --filter @app/web test:storybook. No API/monorepo suite locally. A pre-existing unrelated failure is not fixed out of scope, only reported.

openDecisions.question: 01 §4 allows a tooltip on the truncated secondary name only if the same mechanism naturally supports it. Should it be added?
openDecisions.specSays: 01 §4: 'Add a tooltip for it only if the same small reusable mechanism naturally supports it; do not add extra complexity solely for the secondary line.'
openDecisions.codeSays: The secondary line sits outside the link and under the link's ::after (audit C47). To receive hover it needs relative z-10, and then clicks on that line no longer navigate, which breaks the click-matrix row 'ordinary card body → details'. Moving it inside the link changes the link's accessible name, and the heading's too if it sits inside the h3.
options: A. Skip it.
B. Lift the line with relative z-10 and accept that clicks on it do not navigate.
C. Move the line inside the link.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It does not fit naturally, which is the spec's own condition for adding it.
openDecisions.answer: A, adopted as recommended. No tooltip on the secondary global name; T9 moves to excluded.

assumptions.decision: The stretched link and its focus ring use ::before (before:absolute before:inset-0 before:rounded-xl, focus-visible:before:ring-3) instead of the ::after named in T1/T2.
assumptions.reason: ::after paints after the name span inside the link, so the tooltip trigger span would never receive hover unless it got a z-index, which T1 forbids (only the actions layer may carry one). With ::before the span is plain relative and sits above the pseudo-element; clicks on it still land in the <a>.

assumptions.decision: Compact density keeps the avatar and its initial exactly as today: Avatar size=lg with the original size-14 class (rendered 40px) and a text-xl initial.
assumptions.reason: Avatar size=lg carries data-[size=lg]:size-10, which outranks size-14, so the baseline roster avatar was already 40px (audit C22 read the class, not the rendered size). A first pass shrank the compact initial to text-lg; the a11y audit showed that drops it below WCAG large-text size and fails 4.5:1 against the gradient, so it was reverted. The dead size-14 is follow-up FU2.

assumptions.decision: The secondary global name uses line-clamp-1 wrap-anywhere instead of truncate.
assumptions.reason: truncate (nowrap) puts the full name width into min-content, and the narrow grid track is auto, so a long global name caused horizontal overflow at 390px.
